$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.24,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.24/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 42e6616f497f78a12e0afa812ae2c83c04e0fe0448cd6ee9b82e04847078d9f3 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.24/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
42e6616f497f78a12e0afa812ae2c83c04e0fe0448cd6ee9b82e04847078d9f3 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
